Step 1 – Tautomerism  
• 1,4-Benzoquinone (p-benzoquinone) has no α-hydrogen that can shift to an oxygen atom without changing the total hydrogen count of the molecule; conversion to hydroquinone would require addition of two external hydrogens (a redox process, not a tautomerism).  
• Cyclohexane-1,3,5-trione can tautomerise: each carbonyl has an α-hydrogen and the triple enol form is the aromatic 1,3,5-trihydroxybenzene (phloroglucin).  
⇒ The compound that does NOT exhibit tautomerism is benzoquinone.

Step 2 – Optical isomerism  
• Methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate (methyl lactate) contains the carbon skeleton CH₃–CH(OH)–CO₂Me.  
  – The carbon bearing –OH is attached to four different groups (H, CH₃, OH, CO₂Me), so it is a chiral centre; the molecule exists as a pair of enantiomers and is optically active.  
• Dimethyl fumarate [(E)-dimethyl but-2-enedioate] has an E-alkene but no stereogenic centre, and the molecule possesses a plane of symmetry; it is achiral and hence optically inactive.  
⇒ The compound that shows optical isomerism is methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate.

Combining the two results:  
A = benzoquinone, B = methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate.

Answer: B
